subjects.displayTitle: Preserving the writings: care for the words entrusted to us
subjects.introduction: One wrong letter in a word, and the treatise must be corrected; a Tablet someone claims to have received must be produced, signed in ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s own hand, before anyone believes it. Such exactness treats the Writings as a trust. The verses came, by the amanuensis’s own account, faster than any pen could follow, twelve hundred in an hour, his hand moving of itself, and dispatched without being compared, so that when printing was contemplated no one could tell which variants were revealed and which were scribal. Hence the labour that follows: copies checked against Zayn’s handwriting, correct versions sent out to replace faulty ones, Tablets read again in Bahá’u’lláh’s presence, boxes of papers carried, lost, withheld or recovered, and at the end the promise that the House of Justice would gather the Sacred Writings and scrutinise them. Paul closes a letter to the Thessalonians with a greeting in his own hand as the token by which his letters may be known, a recognisably similar concern [1]. From here the path runs to the transcription and collection of the Writings, the discrepancies that honest copies preserve, and the questions of translation and publication through which the words reach new readers.
subjects.arc: Begin with evidence and careful comparison, follow the work of recording and transmitting revelation, then consider preservation, publication, and responsible reading.

order.why: Read the gathering of accurate writings for the London library.
Keep the reported warning about invented attributed statements distinctly sourced.
shortened: I have come to these parts and I find out that certain people have attributed to me certain statements of which I am innocent. Anybody who has an opinion and desires to circulate it will attribute it to me. Anyone quoting me must have authority written either with my own hand, or tablets signed with my seal. Otherwise, those statements do not belong to me. Every instruction, every teaching that I desire to spread, I will write with my own hand. You must know this generally. Never accept statements without my writing which is signed and sealed - any statement.

order.why: Keep the reported handwriting and amanuensis evidence in its attributed historical setting.
shortened: In a Tablet from the Bab to Yahya and written in Yahya's own handwriting, he is directed by the Bab to ascertain God's intention by asking Siyyid Husayn, the amanuensis.

order.why: Open with a clear criterion for attributed statements.
shortened: Thou hast asked regarding the contribution toward the education of the children of the school of Tarbiat. Cooperation and mutual assistance are the basis of the religion of God. The East must assist the West and the West must assist the East. Whosoever quotes any thing from my tongue ask him an authority either with my pen or with my signature. If he has such an authority in his hand all right, if he has no such authority do not give importance to traditions. Keep always this as a criterion in view.

order.why: Distinguish valid documentary evidence from mere assertion.
Consider the confusion caused by undocumented accounts.
Read careful examination together with the stated interpretive authority.
Notice how a small textual difference demands correction.
Read the distinction between revealed variation and scribal error.
shortened: Many of the copies made by scribes differed from one another. Now people know not which variations from the Most Holy Court were revealed as such, and which arose from the scribes' inattention. What hath been revealed from God is truth without doubt, but since Jinab-i-Nazir (upon him be the Glory of God) wished to print some of the books, We therefore commanded the Greater Branch and this servant in attendance to compare them and submit whatever variations they found, for most people were and are not aware of these matters and are not informed about the nature of revelation.

order.why: Join copying with comparison and verification.
shortened: Regarding what is being sent, it is beloved that copies be made and, after comparison and verification, be given to their owners.

order.why: Hear the concise requirement that distributed copies be correct.
shortened: Whatever is given must be correct. Some copies of the Iqan that exist in this land have not all attained the standard of correctness.

order.why: Consider correction or fresh transcription from a designated copy.
Read the particular instruction to compare a printed book with Zayn’s handwriting.
Retain the assurance concerning the Tablet of the Temple in that hand.
Consider the instruction not to alter a passage that may initially puzzle a reader.
Distinguish an allusion to a verse’s meaning from an intended alteration.
Read attention to intention within the circumstances of a particular treatise.
Consider an argument grounded in the original handwriting.
shortened: This is not a narrative that its narrator could be denied, nor is it in the handwriting of a scribe that could give rise to doubts and result in lack of confidence. Rather, it is by the pen of the Most High.

order.why: Read handwriting, signature, and seal used to test an allegation.
Hear the rejection of falsely attributed named Tablets.
Read the related reported requirement for signed credentials.
shortened: Now that I am leaving you I counsel you not to accept any one coming to you with strange stories attributed to me without first demanding his signed credentials which must be in my handwriting.
Therefore do not credit such statements. Accept nothing purporting to come from me without my signature.

order.why: Retain the reported repetition of that caution.
Consider the reported request to produce the claimed Tablet.
Examine authorship through the account of letters dictated in an attendant’s voice.
shortened: I briefly submit that not a single word was from this servant - all were revealed from the Kingdom of God, my Lord and your Lord and the Lord of all who are in heaven and on earth. At all times, letters that were in this servant's name were, after permission, read in the Most Holy and Most Exalted Presence, and He would command "Take up the pen," and all responses from beginning to end would be revealed from the blessed mouth and recorded.

order.why: Keep the reported clarification and remembered dispute in their historical setting.
Read the brief description of hearing and recording utterance.
shortened: We arose this day and left the house, proceeding to another place. When We arrived, We commanded the servant in attendance before Us, and he heard and wrote down what the Tongue of Grandeur spoke forth in his luminous station.

order.why: Consider the pressure of rapid revelation upon the act of transcription.
Read the reported physical labor and fatigue of writing.
Consider the volume of correspondence and its effect on replies.
Read the many destinations served by the scribe’s work.
Notice the absence of a scribe delaying dispatch.
shortened: Tablets have been revealed in these days and mention made of that person, but since no scribe was available to make copies, they were not sent, until we see what divine destiny will require.

order.why: Read the distinction between revelation script and finished copies.
Consider secretarial address errors alongside the use of signatures and seals.
Keep the reported account of the Iqan’s dictation and dates attributed.
Read the Bab’s account of writings produced within the stated period.
Retain the statement concerning the Book of Joseph and Book of Justice.
shortened: We did indeed change the Book of Joseph [Qayyumu'l-Asma] before, and We sent down the Book of Justice [Kitabu'l-'Adl] thereafter, and verily therein are clear verses for people who believe.

order.why: Read the Bab’s objection to faulty copies and unauthorized changes.
shortened: Those few sections which had been dispatched from Shiraz arrived in a single day, most of them grievously faulty; and in certain passages they have been altered and corrupted. Inform Mulla Sadiq that some of its verses have, without knowledge and without warrant, been changed; and such a thing, in mine own sight, possesseth no authority -- though for the people, one verse thereof, rightly set down, is sufficient.

order.why: Consider the prayer’s account of beautiful material presentation.
shortened: I would have returned unto Thee all the verses, evidences, scriptures and words that Thou hast sent down unto me. Therefore, O my God, bear witness that I have created these letters in the most excellent manner, then fashioned them in the Book, in a mighty and impregnable Book, in the most beautiful script, on the most delicate paper, with the most noble refinement, in the most wondrous and original way.

order.why: Keep the particular Babi instruction about inks within its original scope.
Read the instruction to send a book in golden ink with its accompanying address.
shortened: And send thou likewise this Book unto the King of that region with golden ink that thou mayest be numbered among the helpers of that which is written. And whoso denieth Our verses and departeth not from his house as an emigrant unto the Land of Remembrance - We shall reveal his decree in the Book even as was revealed concerning Abu Lahab in the Qur'an. Fear ye God, O concourse of men, and have mercy upon yourselves, and disgrace not your subjects through what hath been sent down unto you after God's decree, and after all people shall read.

order.why: Consider durable ink, suitable paper, margins, and binding as practical care.
shortened: Thou didst request permission to transcribe a book in thine own hand. It would be most agreeable to me if thou wouldst write two large-format books in clear handwriting, with the utmost perfection, upon very fine and delicate paper of moderate thickness - not thin - and with permanent ink that will not stick together from moisture in the future. Include therein the Tablets of Tarazat, Tajalliyat, Bisharat, Kalimat and Ishraqat. Prepare two copies, and let Jinab-i-'Andalib add delicate illumination, but illuminate only the margins, not the text itself, and prepare very fine bindings.

order.why: Join accurate copying with protection of the original sheet.
Directs correction of a copy against the original revelation text.
Read review in the divine presence together with the need for preservation.
shortened: In these days the revealed Tablets are being read in Our presence, for many Tablets written both before and after were dispatched to various regions without being compared. Therefore, in these days they are repeatedly being read in Our presence, that what God hath intended and what the Tongue of Grandeur hath spoken may become manifest.
The people of God must make a mighty effort to preserve and protect the Tablets.

order.why: Follow Salman’s repeated journeys carrying letters and Tablets.
shortened: From the year 69 until the ascension of Baha'u'llah in 1309 A.H., Salman would arrive once a year, bringing letters, leaving with the Tablets, faithfully delivering each one to him for whom it was intended. Every single year throughout that long period, he came on foot from Persia to Iraq, or to Adrianople, or to the Most Great Prison at 'Akka; came with the greatest eagerness and love, and then went back again.

order.why: Consider trustworthiness in the transmission of correspondence.
shortened: The honored uncle, in the blessed days, served with utmost truthfulness and trustworthiness, and was the means for transmitting Tablets and letters.

order.why: Hear the appreciation of care in recording and dispatch.
shortened: The honored Mirza Mihdi hath been specially favored with God's all-embracing mercy. He hath, at no time, been careless in recording the words of God, nor hath he neglected their dispatch.

order.why: Read postal reliability alongside the statement about two acceptable versions.
Consider urgency, available time, and the means of sending copies.
Read transcription from revelation and the use of numbered lists.
shortened: And, in accordance with the command, this Tablet was revealed from the heaven of His Will; it was transcribed from the original Revelation and sent forth. Likewise were dispatched the numbered lists, in the Name of the Most Great Name, of the Tablets which thou hadst previously requested.

order.why: Join copying with judgment about recipients and circumstances.
Follow the invitation to circulate useful copies onward.
Read the sustained dispatch of verses to many regions.
Consider a newly arrived envelope through the image of a fragrant flower.
Retain the acknowledgment that two packages arrived.
Hear the simple instruction that the packets must not be lost.
shortened: O thou who art beloved! Be ye informed that the Tablets contained in these four packets should not be lost.

order.why: Read the provision of a special volume and the Book of Certitude.
Consider dispatch delayed by wisdom despite completed revelation.
Read the later sending of previously withheld Tablets.
Keep the brief instructions concerning a response and a Tablet to Kalim.
shortened: In response to the person mentioned, a sublime Tablet was revealed and sent.
Additionally, a brief Tablet was written to Kalim - review it and send it.

order.why: Consider a pause in revelation behind a delayed letter.
Read the related account of hesitation during such a pause.
Distinguish outwardly sent answers from answers described as inscribed in God’s Book.
shortened: Some receive answers that are outwardly revealed and sent, while the answers to others are recorded in God's Book and inscribed by the Pen of His bounty.

order.why: Consider scattered laws gathered into a single Tablet.
Read compilation as a means of making glad tidings accessible.
Consider many Tablets as belonging to one book.
Retain the reported description of a distinct body of revelation.
Keep the particular instruction distinguishing Abdu’l-Baha’s writings from divine Tablets.
Consider selecting suitable passages for teaching according to circumstances.
Read the decision to print so that access is not delayed.
Consider publication through time, place, and requirements.
shortened: What they have written regarding the printing of the book is correct and adorned with the ornament of truth. These matters depend upon time, place, occasion and requirements. In all things they must be mindful of wisdom.

order.why: Retain the specific permission to publish a book of addresses.
Keep the stated sequence of publishing Bayan and Aqdas in its historical setting.
Read the particular restriction on a translation within its stated concern about differences.
Retain the reported statement on translation as a historical instruction.
Read selective transmission of marriage laws before wider dissemination.
Keep the marriage-sermon instruction and embedded scribal direction in its source context.
shortened: Likewise, in these days a marriage sermon has been revealed from the heaven of unity. After the consent of both parties and the consent of the parents, they should gather in a place among the God-fearing and recite this blessed sermon with the utmost joy and fragrance. After the recitation of the sermon, the beloved and his beloved should, in a separate place, recite these two blessed verses that were revealed in the Bayan. [The verses mentioned in the Bayan should be written.] Then the husband should deliver the dowry to his wife, and both parties should sign the document, as well as the witnesses.

order.why: Read the specific safeguards governing a seal.
Consider the effort to recover an original Tablet.
shortened: The photographs of the Bab's Tablet have arrived - may thy face be illumined! If thou canst obtain the original Tablet which is in His own handwriting, even if up to five hundred tumans must be paid, it would be most fitting and would constitute a mighty service to the Cause, for that blessed Tablet must not remain in the hands of the people.

order.why: Hear the instruction to preserve recovered writings with reverence.
shortened: The Tablets that belonged to the King of Martyrs and have come into the possession of the friends from strangers - preserve and protect these Tablets with the utmost reverence and honor.

order.why: Keep the reported advice about safe custody and later display tied to its occasion.
Consider the reported recognition of a bequest to a person outside the community.
shortened: Sometimes after my arrival a woman brought to me a big bundle containing all my Epistles written to Mrs Cole. She said: 'Mrs Cole has bequeathed these precious, spiritual letters to me. She considered these to be her greatest possessions. I have now thought to bring them to you. As I am not a Baha'i I would not like to keep them without your permission.' Then I told her, 'Because this was her last wish, I am sure you are the proper person to take care of these epistles.'

order.why: Read the account of entrusted papers and their removal.
shortened: There are several supplementary ordinances in the Blessed Handwriting, but the Covenant-breakers stole 'Abdu'l-Baha's papers and that document was among them. A few days before the Ascension of the Blessed Beauty, may my spirit be sacrificed for His loved ones, He commanded 'Abdu'l-Baha to gather the papers in His blessed chamber and put them in a bag. According to His blessed command, the papers were collected and placed in two bags. He said "These papers are entrusted to you."

order.why: Retain the related account of the casket and its contents.
Read the disputed papers in connection with the direction of prayer.
shortened: This sacred place has been explicitly designated by the Supreme Pen in a special tablet, and that tablet contains other laws as well, all by the Supreme Pen. That tablet was in the blessed case which was entrusted to Abdu'l-Baha before the Ascension. That case contained numerous papers, but the unfaithful ones took it away under some pretext and now it is with them.

order.why: Keep the reported account of custody and possible alteration as an attributed statement.
shortened: As it is, he has appropriated many papers and Tablets written by the Blessed Perfection. It is possible for these writings to be altered, as the meanings in Persian are greatly changed by a single dot here and there. Before His Ascension, the Blessed Perfection said to me, 'I have given You all the papers.' He put them in two satchels and sent them to Me. After His Ascension, Muhammad-'Ali said, 'You had better give me the two satchels to take care of.' He took them away and never returned them.

order.why: Retain the separately reported account of boxes withheld.
shortened: At the time of the ascension of Baha'u'llah, as we were otherwise occupied, I gave him [Mirza Muhammad-'Ali] for safekeeping two boxes containing divine Writings. He has concealed them. He has kept them so that after my passing he might bring them out and use them in accord with his personal inclination.

order.why: Read the reported instruction gathering the writings before Baha’u’llah’s passing.
shortened: A few days before his departure Baha'u'llah called me into his bedroom and commanded me to gather together all his writing and Tablets telling me that 'they shall belong to thee'.

order.why: Keep the reported narrative of collection, collation, loss, and dispute together.
shortened: At the intimation of His Holiness my Master, he transcribed a complete collection---most of it from the handwriting of Aqa Siyyid Husayn---of the writings of His Holiness the Exalted One; and all of it was corrected and collated. With what pains His Holiness my Master had obtained these writings, and at last brought them to 'Akka; but what Mirza Muhammad-'Ali did with them is not known. If such Tablets as these should be lost, it would be a loss to the Cause.

After the Ascension, a committee was formed under the leadership of Mirza Muhammad-'Ali, that the blessed Tablets might be gathered together and authenticated, so that thereafter they might be known and accounted for.
They interfered with and tampered with the writings of the Blessed Beauty, and exerted themselves that I should be slain.

order.why: Read the allegation about copied writings and a seal in its polemical setting.
shortened: At the time of emergence from between Gog and Magog, who were two idolaters, I sent a box containing blessed writings of the Exalted One and Aqa Siyyid Husayn, along with His seal, to that one who turned away from God. And in the early years of the new Cause, for four years We commanded him to copy from the writings of His Holiness, such that now writings of that apostate in the style of His Holiness exist. In these days he hath begun using those same writings and writing whatever Satan inspires in him, sealing it with His Holiness's seal and showing it to vile souls like himself.

order.why: Keep the particular warning about protecting the Bab’s books in its historical address.
shortened: O Muhammad-Rafi' Dawlatabadi and those with him have intended to steal the Book of God - that is, the Persian Bayan and Ahsanul-Qisas. Since these two clear Books are adorned with utterances that give glad tidings to all of the appearance of the Great Announcement, they have therefore intended to destroy them. It is obligatory and incumbent upon all the friends of Truth that whosoever possesses them should preserve them and guard them from this rebellious and transgressing band.

order.why: Read the reported account of a disputed Tablet and later scrutiny distinctly attributed.
Consider consolation after loss through the image of the Preserved Tablet.
Close with the relation between revealed verses, proof, and future divine authority.
shortened: Until this Manifestation, verses alone have been proof for all, for We had sent down this decree in all previous Books.

Although in this Manifestation all signs of power, manifest proofs, wondrous verses, glorious manifestations and divine attributes have appeared - and all this as a grace from Us to all created things - yet henceforth the matter resteth in God's hands, that He may designate what shall be proof for future Manifestations.

questions: Why might reverence for a sacred text require close attention to copies, handwriting, attribution, and context?
How can readers distinguish a documented instruction from a remembered report or an appealing story?
What do these passages reveal about the labor and judgment involved in preserving and circulating writings?
How does the handwritten greeting in 2 Thessalonians 3:17–18 illuminate the role of recognizable evidence in religious communication?
What should be considered when a text contains variants, difficult wording, or instructions addressed to a particular time and place?
How might present-day readers and compilers combine wider access with fidelity to the words and authority of their sources?

references.note: The closing greeting presents Paul’s own hand as a distinguishing token and concludes with a blessing. Compare this textual attention to recognizable authorship with the compilation’s concern for signed evidence and trustworthy transmission. The comparison does not settle historical questions about any manuscript’s authenticity.

subjects.displayTitle: Praying for victory: steadfastness, justice, and transformed hearts
subjects.introduction: Victory, Bahá’u’lláh testifies in the middle of a prayer, is His loved ones being aided to know God and enabled to remember and praise Him. The definition is startling from a community that was captive, scattered and persecuted. In the same breath He asks that His enemies be aided to return to God; ‘Abdu’l-Bahá begs that those who wronged Him have their diseases healed and the veils lifted from their eyes; triumph is sought through love and the light of the teachings rather than through contention. None of this silences the anguish. Bábí and Bahá’í prayers alike cry out against oppressors, call on the Avenger, and ask for judgment, and those cries keep their own settings. Alongside them stand petitions for wisdom, and a confidence that the fruits of service lie far beyond what any present generation can see. Paul’s counsel in Romans, leaving vengeance to God while feeding a hungry enemy and overcoming evil with good, holds the same tension within a few verses [1]. The way continues into rendering assistance to God, the meaning of victory itself, and the growth of the Cause.
subjects.arc: Begin with victory as remembrance and transformed hearts, hear the prayers of vulnerable communities, then explore divine judgment, human service, and confidence in an unfolding future.

order.why: Read conquest expressly through love and the illumination of teachings.
shortened: O Thou Incomparable God! O Thou Lord of the Kingdom! These souls are Thy heavenly army. Assist them and, with the cohorts of the Supreme Concourse, make them victorious, so that each one of them may become like unto a regiment and conquer these countries through the love of God and the illumination of divine teachings.

O God! Be Thou their supporter and their helper, and in the wilderness, the mountain, the valley, the forests, the prairies and the seas, be Thou their confidant---so that they may cry out through the power of the Kingdom and the breath of the Holy Spirit.

order.why: Open with the explicit description of victory as knowing, remembering, and praising God.
shortened: O Lord! Seize them through Thy power, then aid Thy loved ones through Thy loving-kindness and Thy handmaidens through Thy grace. I testify at this moment that victory is their being aided to know Thee and enabled to remember and praise Thee.

order.why: Read a prayer asking that enemies return to God.
Hear the plea against oppression together with the request for opponents’ healing and guidance.
Consider assistance to the Cause through wisdom.
shortened: Say: My God, my God! Aid Thy servants to assist Thy Cause through the wisdom which Thou hast sent down in Thy perspicuous Book.

order.why: Join steadfastness with wisdom and utterance.
shortened: I beseech Thee by those who have quaffed the wine of supreme steadfastness before the faces of all peoples, to assist me in all conditions to help Thy Cause and exalt Thy Word and to manifest that which Thou hast commanded me in Thy Tablets with wisdom and utterance.

order.why: Read protection of the Afnan together with wise remembrance.
shortened: O Lord! Protect Thy Afnan from the evil of Thine enemies who have disbelieved in Thy proof, turned away from Thy Manifestation and Thy signs, and ordain for each one of them to assist Thy Cause among Thy creation and to make mention of Thee with wisdom and utterance before the people of Thy realm.

order.why: Distinguish fidelity during trials from allegiance after victory.
shortened: When the victory arriveth, every man shall profess himself a believer and shall hasten to the shelter of God’s Faith. Happy are they who in the days of world-encompassing trials have stood fast in the Cause and refused to swerve from its truth.

order.why: Hear powerlessness acknowledged in a prayer for loved ones.
Read the desire for weakness to become strength.
Consider sorrow transformed into joy.
shortened: I beseech Thee by Thy Self to manifest through Thy sovereignty that which shall transform sorrow into joy and abasement into glory.

order.why: Hear the lament of believers facing oppression in many places.
shortened: Thou seest, O my God, how Thy loved ones have been encompassed by the rebellious amongst Thy creatures and the wicked amidst Thy people. No land remaineth but the lamentation of Thy lovers and the wailing of Thy chosen ones were lifted up therein. I beseech Thee by Thy Most Great Name to draw forth the hand of power from the bosom of Thy might and to assist therewith all them that love Thee.

order.why: Read the account of families driven from their homeland.
shortened: O my God! Thou seest and knowest that the oppressors have wronged Thy loved ones who have turned toward the Dayspring of Thy Revelation, the Dawning-Place of Thine inspiration and the Source of Thy Cause, and have driven them, together with their children and their women, from their homeland - though they had manifested naught except that which Thou didst command them through Thy Most Exalted Pen. I beseech Thee, O my Lord, by Thy Most Glorious Name, to send down from the heaven of Thy bounty that which shall exalt the believers and abase the ungodly.

order.why: Consider the vulnerability of scattered teachers and the request for a smoother path.
shortened: My God, my God! Thou seest Thy sincere servants scattered throughout the regions, and beholdest Thy assured bondsmen dispersed in all directions among the heedless, calling people to the fountainhead of certitude, guiding them to the Straight Path, and giving them to drink from the Spring of Tasneem. Yet the opponents shoot at them with penetrating arrows and attack them like ravening wolves and fierce beasts, making them taste grievous torment. O Lord! Aid them with hosts from Thy glorious Kingdom, support them with Thy wondrous favor, assist them with Thy manifest sovereignty, and make smooth their path, O my Glorious Lord!

order.why: Hear the sheep-and-wolves image as a prayer for assistance.
shortened: O Lord! Thou seest how the wolves have seized Thy sheep, through whom the rain of Thy mercy hath poured forth from the clouds of Thy generosity. I beseech Thee to assist Thy party through the hosts of the seen and the unseen. Verily Thou art God, the Almighty, the All-Compelling, the Mighty, the Unconstrained.

order.why: Read the plea for strength beneath oppression.
Consider continued turning toward revelation amid severe trials.
shortened: Put forth, therefore, out of the bosom of Thy glory, O my Lord, the hand of Thine omnipotence, and through it assist Thou Thy loved ones who, though sore-tried in Thy path with such trials as have caused the inmates of the kingdom of Thy Cause to groan, were not deterred from turning towards the horizon of Thy Revelation.

order.why: Join a cry for deliverance with holding fast to loving-kindness.
Keep the unfinished invocation’s sense of vulnerability in its original wording.
Read lament and the appeal to the light of justice together.
shortened: Say: Glory be to Thee, O Thou Who art the Goal of the hearts of them that know Thee and the Object of worship of all who are in the heavens and on earth! Thou seest how darkness hath encompassed all lands to such extent that Thy party among Thy servants lamenteth. O my Lord! I beseech Thee by the lights of the Day-Star of Thy justice and the splendors of the Sun of Thy Word to ordain through Thy Most Exalted Pen for those who have turned to Thee, O Thou Owner of Names, that which Thou didst ordain for Thy loved ones and chosen ones.

order.why: Hear deliverance sought through remembered sacred narratives.
shortened: I beseech Thee by the light whereby Thou didst deliver Noah and his companions, and didst make the fire cool for Thy Friend despite his enemies, and whereby Thou didst manifest Thy straight path and make it the herald of Thy mighty News, to deliver them through Thy grace and bounty.

order.why: Read the Bab’s prison prayer for truthful judgment and release.
Consider service sought in remembrance of bloodshed and suffering.
Read steadfastness and praise in response to the suffering of loved ones.
Hear the supplicant among enemies asking to continue serving.
Consider the desire not to be left to oneself in affliction.
Read the captive’s petition for firm feet and spreading light.
Keep humility and contrition alongside the forceful request for aid.
shortened: O my God! I press my brow and cover my face with the dust of lowliness, impotence and contrition, beseeching Thee at eventide and at dawn, supplicating before Thee in the darkness of night and the bright light of day, that Thou mayest assist Thy servant, who hath turned unto Thee in humility and submission and repentance, with the hosts of power and might and the armies of glory and dominion against every aggressive doubter and sinner mentioned in the Book and every contemptible impostor from among the people of the veil.

order.why: Read personal confession together with prayer for a community’s strength.
Consider preservation, fidelity, and victory within the same petition.
Hear the request for victory and the good of both lives.
shortened: Render Thy Cause victorious, O my Lord, and abase Thou Thine enemies. Write down, then, for us the good of this life and of the life to come. Thou art the Truth, Who knoweth the secret things. No God is there but Thee, the Ever-Forgiving, the All-Bountiful.

order.why: Read triumph joined to steadfast service.
Consider the prayer for divine assistance and manifested power.
shortened: O Lord! I beseech Thee by Thy power which hath encompassed all things, that Thou assist these souls with the wonders of Thy succor, strengthen them through Thy might, and make them victorious over Thine enemies, that thereby the manifestations of Thy power may appear among Thy servants and the revelations of Thy might among Thy creatures.

order.why: A supplication for divine assistance and the exaltation of the Cause.
Keep the account of captivity and imprisonment within the petition.
Read the invocations of divine restraint, subduing, and chastisement in their prayerful setting.
shortened: Glorified art Thou, O Lord my God! I beseech Thee by Thy Name, the Restrainer, to withhold from us the maleficence of Thine adversaries who have disbelieved in Thy testimony, and caviled at Thy beauty. Overpower by Thy Name, the All-Subduing, such as have wronged Thy Previous Manifestation Who hath now appeared invested with Thy title, the All-Glorious. Lay hold, by Thy name, the Chastiser, on them that have treated Thy Cause with scorn, have jested at Thy most mighty utterances, and were hindered from attaining this most exalted station. Enable Thy loved ones, by Thy Name, the Victorious, to prevail against Thine enemies and the infidels among Thy creatures.

order.why: Hear the petition for judgment as addressed to God.
shortened: Well-beloved is Thy mercy unto the sincere among Thy servants, and well-beseeming Thy chastisement of the infidels among Thine enemies. Send down upon them, therefore, O my Lord, that which will unmistakably reveal unto them the fury of Thy wrath and the ascendancy of Thy power, and will enable them to recognize the weight of Thy might and the greatness of Thy strength.

order.why: Keep the appeal to the Avenger alongside the recognition of God’s enduring presence.
Retain the brief petition concerning those following self and desire.
Read the severe imagery as a petition against oppression in its source’s voice.
shortened: O Lord! Cut off the hands that were stretched forth against them in tyranny and oppression, and the tongues that were extended against them in hatred and enmity. Then turn back upon them what they intended against those who sought the Dayspring of Thy Revelation and the Dawning-Place of Thy inspiration.

order.why: Consider the desire that violence cease to afflict the land and its people.
shortened: Send down upon them, O my Lord, what will cause them to be busied with each others' concerns. Let, then, their violence be confined to their own selves, that the land and they that dwell therein may find peace.

order.why: Retain the prayer’s uncompromising language of purification and praise.
Read the related petition concerning rejection and divine decree.
Keep the request to exalt loved ones and abase enemies in its original form.
shortened: O my Lord! I beseech Thee by what Thou art, to send down from the right hand of Thy power that which shall exalt Thy loved ones and abase Thine enemies.

order.why: Read the Bab’s invocation of judgment and aid together.
shortened: Therefore, O God, seize Thine enemies with the assaults of Thy wrath, and aid Thy chosen ones with the breezes of Thy glory. There is no God but Thee, and no Mighty One besides Thee.

order.why: Retain the Bab’s prayer for punishment and favor in its historical religious setting.
shortened: I beseech God to inflict the severest punishment upon those who acted proudly against You and transgressed against You, for He is most severe in might and in retribution. May God bestow favor upon those who were guided by Your guidance, and may He grant, through His grace and mercy, His good pleasure to those who are pleased with Your good pleasure, as befits His supreme generosity and bounty, for He is the Munificent, the Inaccessible.

order.why: Read the sustained Babi invocation of requital without turning it into a human command.
Keep the prayer of negation’s letter symbolism and severe language intact.
Read the Friday prayer within its stated Babi setting.
Retain the prayer’s language of vengeance and divine sovereignty.
Keep the particular petition for a powerful sovereign in its original setting.
Read the Babi prayer’s wide range of divine attributes and its source omission.
Move through the image of life’s scattered forces gathering against darkness.
shortened: O Lord! Make me and Thy sincere servants as hosts arrayed from Thy most glorious Kingdom and as bands scattered against the parties that oppose the Supreme Concourse, until the ranks of the army of death are scattered and the disheveled forces of life are gathered together, and the power of the rays shining from the realm of light rends asunder the veils of darkness, and the lights of Thy brilliant morn and manifest dawn spread over all regions.

order.why: Hear the concise prayer for light’s victory.
shortened: Therefore, O Lord of Hosts, confirm us so that the army of light may achieve victory and the forces of darkness may be defeated.

order.why: Read the Covenant prayer’s martial imagery in its devotional voice.
shortened: O Lord! Make me a herald of the Covenant, and a piercing flame against the people of discord, and an arrow penetrating the breast of the hypocrites, and a light shining throughout all regions.

order.why: Consider blessing, preservation, and the diffusion of light.
Read the company made verses of unity and banners of praise.
shortened: Through the hosts of the Supreme Concourse make that faithful company victorious and triumphant, and favor them with abundant grace. Make them verses of unity and banners of glorification, and day by day increase their confirmation.

order.why: Consider servants, trustees, guardians, and bearers of Tablets as forms of assistance.
Read practical work on a house of worship as a focus of prayer.
shortened: O God! O God! Verily, I implore Thee with throbbing heart and streaming tears to aid every one who endeavors for the erection of this edifice, in the building of a house, wherein Thy Name is mentioned every morn and eve.
Verily, Thou art the Generous, the Merciful, the Bountiful!

order.why: Extend assistance to those who help the loved ones.
shortened: O Lord! Aid Thou Thy loved ones, and them that aid them.

order.why: Hear the brief request for aid to one who seeks God.
shortened: O my God! Glory be unto Thee! Aid, then, O my God, him who hath loved Thee and hath sought Thy face.

order.why: Retain the shared prayer for aid to the supplicant and companions.
shortened: O Lord! Aid me and those with me through Thy sovereignty and might, for verily Thou art powerful over whatsoever Thou willest.

order.why: Read the concise appeal for divine succor.
shortened: I implore Thee, O Thou Who holdest in Thy hands the reins of unconstrained power, to succor them through the wondrous potency of Thy might.

order.why: Hear the request for hosts of power and might.
Consider the prayer for wondrous assistance.
shortened: I beseech Thee by Thy Name which hath conquered all names and encompassed all who are in earth and heaven, to assist Thy loved ones through the wonders of Thy victory.

order.why: Join aid to the fruits of the Tree of Oneness.
shortened: I beseech Thee by Thy Name through which Thy Beauty was made manifest, and Thy proof did shine forth, and Thy names did appear, and Thy Dove did warble, and then Thy Most Great Name and Thy Most Ancient Beauty were upraised, to exalt Thy Cause and to aid Thy loved ones, and to bestow upon them from the fruits of the Tree of Thy Oneness and the produce of the holy Tree of Thy Singleness.

order.why: Read the exaltation of those who hold fast to God.
shortened: We beseech Thee, O God of the world and Goal of the nations, to send down from the heaven of Thy power that which will exalt the station of those among Thy servants who profess Thy unity and those among Thy creatures who hold fast to Thee.

order.why: Keep the petition for the people of T and F without inventing expanded place names.
Consider assurance and gladness as desired fruits.
shortened: I beseech Thee by the ocean of Thy knowledge and the heaven of Thy Word and the sun of Thy power to manifest in the world that which will gladden the eyes of Thy loved ones and bring assurance to their hearts in Thy days.

order.why: Read nearness, praise, and remembrance together.
shortened: O Lord! Deprive us not of the wonders of Thy grace in Thy days, and distance us not from the shores of nearness through Thy bounty and favors.
O Lord! Send down upon me that which will make me rich through Thy riches, and speaking in Thy praise, and mindful in Thy remembrance. Then ordain for me what Thou hast ordained for Thy chosen ones.

order.why: Consider the movement from vain imaginings toward confidence and certitude.
shortened: I entreat Thee, O my God, by Thy Name which irradiateth all things, to raise up such servants as shall incline their ears to the voice of the melodies that hath ascended from the right hand of the throne of Thy glory. Make them, then, to quaff from the hand of Thy grace the wine of Thy mercy, that it may assure their hearts, and cause them to turn away from the left hand of idle fancies and vain imaginings to the right hand of confidence and certitude.

order.why: Hear the prayer for quickened hearts ready to carry a message.
shortened: Assist Thou Thy servants, O my God, to help Thy Cause, and give them to drink what will quicken their hearts in Thy realm, lest anything hinder them from remembering Thee and from extolling Thy virtues, that they may quit their homes in Thy name, and summon all the multitudes unto Thee.

order.why: Read service as response to grace received without merit.
Retain the petition for the particular person mentioned in a Tablet.
shortened: Then cause to succeed, O my God, him whom We have desired to mention in this Tablet and assist him to aid Thy Cause and exalt Thy Word.

order.why: Consider becoming helpers of religion and supporters of loved ones.
Hear the raising of guidance’s standards.
shortened: O my Lord! Aid them in that whereby the standards of Thy guidance and the banners of Thy Cause shall be upraised.

order.why: Read aid directed toward the signs of triumph.
shortened: I beseech Thee, O God of all beings and Educator of all created things, to aid Thy loved ones to that which shall cause the standards of Thy triumph and victory to be raised amidst Thy creation.

order.why: Consider confirmation in assistance and the exaltation of the Word.
Join remembrance, nearness, and victory in a personal prayer.
Read the wish to be counted among those who arose to serve.
Hear the petition to arise for the Cause’s triumph.
Consider the declared aim of exalting the Word.
shortened: By Thy might, O God of the world and Goal of the nations, I have desired naught but the exaltation of Thy Word and the manifestation of Thy Cause.

order.why: Read the prayer that a helper may arise.
Retain the related appeal for one who will aid the Cause.
Consider assistance sought through a person possessing power.
Read the future scope of service through the example of the apostles.
shortened: Consider! The station and the confirmation of the apostles in the time of Christ was not known, and no one looked on them with the feeling of importance--nay, rather, they persecuted and ridiculed them. Later on it became evident what crowns studded with the brilliant jewels of guidance were placed on the heads of the apostles, Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of John.
The range of your future achievements still remains undisclosed. I fervently hope that in the near future the whole earth may be stirred and shaken by the results of your achievements.

order.why: Consider spiritual education as the form of prevailing described here.
shortened: Likewise didst thou ask whether, in this Baha'i Dispensation, the spiritual will ultimately prevail. It is certain that spirituality will defeat materialism, that the heavenly will subdue the human, and that through divine education the masses of mankind generally will take great steps forward in all degrees of life---except for those who are blind and deaf and mute and dead.

order.why: Read the dawn and noon as images of unfolding influence.
shortened: This, however, is but the beginning of the dawn, and the heat of the rising Orb of Truth is not yet at the fullness of its power. Once the sun hath mounted to high noon, its fires will burn so hot as to stir even the creeping things beneath the earth; and although it is not for them to behold the light, yet will they all be set in frenzied motion by the impact of the heat.

order.why: Consider gradual growth and latent capacities becoming visible.
shortened: Now in this world of being, the Hand of Divine Power hath firmly laid the foundations of this all-highest Bounty and this wondrous Gift. Gradually whatsoever is latent in the innermost of this Holy Cycle shall appear and be made manifest, for now is but the beginning of its growth and the dayspring of the revelation of its Signs. Ere the close of this Century and of this Age, it shall be made clear and manifest how wondrous was that Springtide and how heavenly was that Gift!

order.why: Retain the distinction of an originating century within the source’s vision.
shortened: In the ages to come, though the Cause of God may rise and grow a hundredfold and the shade of the Sadratu’l-Muntaha shelter all mankind, yet this present century shall stand unrivalled, for it hath witnessed the breaking of that Morn and the rising of that Sun.

order.why: Read the sacred flame’s influence extending beyond its point of origin.
shortened: The fire lit by mortal hand imparteth light and warmth to but a little space, whereas that sacred flame which the Hand of God hath kindled, though burning in the east, will set aflame the west and give warmth to both the north and the south; nay, it shall rise from this world to glow with the hottest flame in the realms on high, flooding with light the Kingdom of eternal glory.

order.why: Close the linked readings with the image of approaching daybreak.
Read the supplied account of responsibility amid confidence in eventual success.
shortened: This shows that we will ultimately succeed. But could we not through our shortcomings, failures to sacrifice and reluctance to concentrate our efforts in spreading the Cause, retard the realization of that ideal. And what would that mean? It shall mean that we will be held responsible before God, that the race will remain longer in its state of waywardness, that wars would not be soon averted, that human suffering will last longer.

order.why: End with the supplied affirmation of endurance through future reverses and trials.

questions: How does victory understood as remembrance and knowledge differ from victory understood only as defeating an opponent?
What do these prayers reveal about vulnerability, grief, and hope under oppression?
How can readers attend honestly to petitions for requital alongside prayers for an enemy’s guidance and return?
What does Romans 12:19–21 contribute to the distinction between divine judgment and the reader’s own conduct?
How might wisdom, loving service, and steadfastness express assistance to a Cause amid opposition?
What responsibilities remain when confidence in a distant fulfillment meets the immediate suffering of others?
