Compare this conjunction with the prayers for judgment, protection, and an enemy’s return here, and with the connected subject’s teaching about assistance through wisdom and hearts rather than contention.

subjects.displayTitle: Higher and lower natures: the direction of a human life
subjects.introduction: How lofty a station a human being can reach, Bahá’u’lláh exclaims, and to what depths he can sink, lower than the meanest creature ever fell. Both possibilities live in the same soul. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calls it the end of night and the beginning of day, a reality poised on the line between darkness and light, bearing an animal side and an angelic side, able to fly through the air by its own devices and to turn those same devices to slaughter. The lower nature shows itself in untruth, cruelty and injustice; the higher in love, mercy, kindness, truth and justice; and the question of a life is which of the two will prevail. The answer is not contempt for the body. A person needs two wings, material and spiritual, and flight is impossible with one. It is education, habit, reflection and the help of God that let intellect govern desire instead of serving it. Paul set the works of the flesh against the fruit of the Spirit, love and patience and gentleness and self-restraint, in the same spirit [1]. Whoever follows this subject will be led on to the nature of the human soul, to the meaning of original sin, to what sets a human being apart from the animal, and to the difference between sight and insight.
subjects.arc: Begin with the soul’s contrasting possibilities, identify the virtues by which growth is recognized, and explore education, habit, spiritual nourishment, and the integration of human capacities.

order.why: Identify the higher nature through love, mercy, truth, and justice.
shortened: In man there are two natures; his spiritual or higher nature and his material or lower nature. In one he approaches God, in the other he lives for the world alone. Signs of both these natures are to be found in men. In his material aspect he expresses untruth, cruelty and injustice; all these are the outcome of his lower nature. The attributes of his Divine nature are shown forth in love, mercy, kindness, truth and justice, one and all being expressions of his higher nature.

order.why: Open with the range between human nobility and degradation.
shortened: How lofty is the station which man, if he but choose to fulfill his high destiny, can attain! To what depths of degradation he can sink, depths which the meanest of creatures have never reached!

order.why: Balance moral contrast with the necessity of two wings.
shortened: For man two wings are necessary. One wing is physical power and material civilization; the other is spiritual power and divine civilization. With one wing only, flight is impossible.

order.why: Read the related account of developing both powers.
shortened: Man has two powers; and his development, two aspects. One power is connected with the material world, and by it he is capable of material advancement. The other power is spiritual, and through its development his inner, potential nature is awakened. These powers are like two wings. Both must be developed, for flight is impossible with one wing.

order.why: Consider bodily strength serving spiritual power and justice.
Join outward education with inward refinement.
shortened: The purport of our subject is that, just as man is in need of outward education, he is likewise in need of ideal refinement; just as the outer sense of sight is necessary to him, he should also possess insight and conscious perception; as he needs hearing, at the same time memory is essential; as a body is indispensable to him, likewise a mind is requisite; one is a material virtue, the other is ideal.

order.why: Read the human station through the image of night becoming day.
shortened: Man is in the ultimate degree of materiality and the beginning of spirituality, that is, he is at the end of imperfection and the beginning of perfection. He is at the furthermost degree of darkness and the beginning of the light. That is why the station of man is said to be the end of night and the beginning of day, meaning that he encompasses all the degrees of imperfection and that he potentially possesses all the degrees of perfection. He has both an animal side and an angelic side; and the role of the educator is to so train human souls that the angelic side may overcome the animal.

order.why: Retain the concise contrast between moral growth and degradation.
Consider humanity’s place at the meeting of ascent and descent.
shortened: Man, however, hath a twofold station: one luminous, the other dark; one pertaining to the realm of the Divine, the other to the world of nature; one inclined towards heavenly virtues, the other towards satanic qualities. For man standeth on the demarcation line between light and darkness. In the circle of existence, he is situated at the lowest point, which marketh at once the end of the arc of descent and the beginning of the arc of ascent.

order.why: Explore the rational soul as the confluence of two seas.
shortened: From one vantage point it possesses spiritual refinement while from the other it exhibits the crassness of carnality, animalistic traits and worldly characteristics. It is neither an absolute abstraction nor is it completely of the world but is the confluence of two seas (majma' al-bahrayn) and a barzakh ("barrier", "isthmus") between two realities (amrayn). If the spiritual aspect dominates it becometh lofty, luminous, merciful, tranquil (mutma'inna), contented (radiya) and approved (mardiyya). And if it is contaminated with contingent, worldly concerns, it becometh immersed in the ocean of darknessess, reproachful (lawwama), commanding to evil (ammara) and residing in the nethermost regions of the world of existence.

order.why: Read the distinction among spirit, mind, and the soul’s two phases.
shortened: The spirit is the power of life, the mind is the power which apprehendeth the reality of things, and the soul is an intermediary between the Supreme Concourse (or Spiritual World) and the lower concourse (or material world). It, i.e., the soul, hath two phases: The higher aspireth to the Kingdom of El-Baha, and the light of the mind shine forth from the horizon (or kingdom) unto its higher sphere; the other phase inclineth to the lower concourse of the material world and its lowest sphere is enveloped in the darkness of ignorance.

order.why: Join inventive capacity with the possibility of virtue or vice.
shortened: His body is heavy, but he flies through the air by means of vehicles of his own devising. His movement is slow, but he journeys rapidly through East and West by the aid of the devices which he has fashioned. In short, this power encompasses all things.

But this human spirit has two aspects: one divine and one satanic--that is, it is capable of both the greatest perfection and the greatest deficiency. Should it acquire virtues it is the noblest of all things and should it acquire vices it becomes the most vile.

order.why: Consider the threefold account alongside the twofold descriptions.
shortened: On the other hand, we find in him justice, sincerity, faithfulness, knowledge, wisdom, illumination, mercy and pity, coupled with intellect, comprehension, the power to grasp the realities of things and the ability to penetrate the truths of existence. All these great perfections are to be found in man. Therefore, we say that man is a reality which stands between light and darkness. From this standpoint his nature is threefold: animal, human and divine. The animal nature is darkness; the heavenly is light in light.

order.why: Read the reported pairs of qualities and capacities.
shortened: There are two sides to man. One is divine, the other worldly; one is luminous, the other dark; one is angelic, the other diabolic. In all sensuous conditions man is equal to the animals, for all animal characteristics exist in him. Likewise, divine and satanic qualities are contained in man; knowledge and ignorance; guidance and error; truth and falsehood; generosity and avarice; valor and timidity; inclination towards God and tendency towards Satan.

order.why: Retain the separately reported enumeration of opposing tendencies.
Keep the reported comparison across creation in its philosophical setting.
Read the reported account of human moral uncertainty and possibility.
Consider the reported image of one condition displacing its opposite.
Explains the need for guidance to rise beyond the lower nature.
Read divine attraction and continual development as an upward influence.
shortened: There exist in man two powers. One power uplifts him. This is divine attraction, which causes man's elevation. In all grades of existence he will develop through this power. This belongs to the spirit. The other power causes man to descend. This is the animal nature. The first attracts man to the Kingdom. The second brings him down to the contingent world. Now we must consider which of these will gain more power. If the heavenly power overcome, man will become heavenly, enlightened, merciful; but if the worldly power overcome, he will be dark, satanic, and like the animal.

order.why: Retain the public address’s contrast of prevailing tendencies.
Consider the effect of closing mind and heart to spiritual blessing.
Keep the reported statement about body and spirit in its own attribution.
Read the reported distinction between inspiration and enslavement to desire.
shortened: The meaning is this: Man has two natures-a higher nature, which is Divine, and a lower nature, which is human. The higher nature is the inspiration of God within us; the lower nature is the slave of sensuous pleasure, desire, attachment, and ignorance.

order.why: Recognize the conflict between spiritual longing and the commanding self.
shortened: How often it happens that the spirit seeks sanctification and the soul of souls yearns, but the commanding self gains control and afflicts man with a movement that causes the spirit to become troubled.

order.why: Read self-mastery through the image of captivity.
shortened: It is evident that the dominion of the self over man is like the rule of an overwhelming sovereignty, and we are captive in its grip and under its chains, shackles and fetters.

order.why: Consider how the insistent self can obscure awareness of its influence.
Hear the concise reported definition of Satan as the insistent self.
Ask whether intellect directs desire or becomes its instrument.
Read the reported formation of a dominant routine of thought.
shortened: This passionate personal ego takes the reins from his hands, crowds out the qualities of the divine ego and changes him into an animal, a creature unable to judge good from evil, or to distinguish light from darkness. He becomes blind to divine attributes, for this acquired individuality, the result of an evil routine of thought becomes the dominant note of his life.

order.why: Consider the reported self’s changing preoccupations.
shortened: When the self gains mastery over man, it brings every affliction upon him. For a time it casts him into thoughts of leadership, for a time into thoughts of vice and immorality, for a time into thoughts of falsehood and hypocrisy, for a time into deception, for a time into thoughts of worldliness and wealth - every hour brings a different affliction.

order.why: Distinguish outward conquest from inward freedom.
Keep the reported Adam-and-Eve symbolism and bribed-mayor example in its setting.
Read the commanding self in relation to unchecked desire and human destructiveness.
shortened: Man like unto the animal is the captive of the world of nature and the laws of nature exercise full control over his nature. He cannot even be compared to the beasts of prey.
If an animal tears another animal, it is only for its daily food but man destroys one hundred thousand souls in one day.

What is written concerning the "ego which is always inclined to do evil" is no other than the fermentation of the passionate desires in the breast of man and the complete, unchecked sway of the carnal and natural forces over him.

order.why: Keep the reported comparison with predatory animals as a moral argument.
Consider the reported intensification of cruelty through human powers.
Read the wartime description of destructive passion in its context.
Retain the reported account of nature, self-love, and political conflict.
shortened: What are passion, desire and the commanding self? These are the exigencies of the natural world. This is not something imaginary - nature itself is the commanding self. If you leave a child in its natural state without education, it remains animal-like. The requirements of nature lead to the commission of every blameworthy act.

Among nature's demands is the struggle for survival. Among nature's demands is self-love. Among nature's demands is anger. Among nature's demands are cunning and deception. Among nature's demands is domination.

order.why: Read the reported claim about nature beside its appeal to transforming faith.
shortened: Now the world of nature has no will power. Man acts according to the requirements of nature. In the world of nature there is treachery and deceit. Consider what the cat does with the mouse, and the fox does with its prey. In the world of nature there is separation, there is the struggle for existence. These are the natural tendencies. This is irresistible.
"That which saves man from the world of nature is the Power of God. It is faith. It is the Fear of God and it will make man an angel; it transforms him.

order.why: Consider divine education as a source of transformed conduct.
shortened: When we look at nature we see pride and arrogance, tyranny and evil, imperfection and deficiency, inequity and transgression, ferocity and bloodthirstiness, causing shame and embarrassment. But the divine law abrogates the law of nature and nullifies the vices of base natures, and legislates true virtues so that through divine education the human world may be illumined, satanic whisperings may be transformed into merciful breathings, the utmost abasement will become the essence of glory, and supreme chastisement will be changed into endless mercy.

order.why: Read the reported rescue from vice through the development of virtues.
shortened: The state of manis nature is injustice, butchery, tyranny, treachery, lechery, achievement of selfish motives, neglect of God and fulfillment of carnal desires. The sanctified Manifestations of God rescue humanity from this black pit and guide them to the highest stations of spirituality. Thereupon, man gains faith, attraction to the divine fragrance, the ability to discover mysteries, divine recognition, knowledge of hidden secrets, trustworthiness, fidelity, charity, nobility and spirituality.

order.why: Identify the positive qualities named as the fruits of spiritual predominance.
Hear love, kindness, and mercy described as befitting humanity.
Read the reported transformation of aggression into loving-kindness.
shortened: If the soul remains in this station and moves along these paths it will be the recipient of this darkness; but if it becomes the recipient of the graces of the world of mind, its darkness will be transformed into light, its tyranny into justice, its ignorance into wisdom, its aggression into loving kindness; until it reach the apex.

order.why: Consider good thoughts, deeds, and love as the polishing of a mirror.
shortened: Those who live thinking good thoughts, doing good deeds, and with love in their hearts -the minds of these become ever clearer, reflecting more and more perfectly the love of God, while the minds of those who live in ignorance and desire are clouded and obscured and give forth His light but meagrely.

order.why: Turn the inquiry toward service and cherishing humanity.
Read the reported encouragement toward character and universal brotherhood.
Keep the reported emphasis on early education and habits in its setting.
shortened: But if these supreme precautions are not taken in the earliest stages of the child's growth, it will be most difficult to curb later on his growing manifold appetites. For then he will live according to the requirements of the world of nature and uncontrolled self. Once the lower and sensual habits of nature take hold of him, it will be very hard to reform him by any human agencies.

order.why: Read the response within its reported story about reputation and the lower self.
Retain the reported account linking restraint and trustworthiness.
shortened: Cruelty is inherent in human nature - if one refrains from it, it is either due to the fear of God or fear of punishment. Otherwise cruelty, oppression, and transgression are inherent in human nature, and the first sign of faith is trustworthiness.

order.why: Hear the related reported role of divine teaching.
shortened: Nature inclines toward evil, unless divine teachings prevent and intervene.

order.why: Keep the reported account of release from lower tendencies attributed.
Read the short reported statement concerning restraint in its original voice.
Consider the reported capacity to overcome a lower tendency.
shortened: However man is endowed by the Creator with a second nature which is supernatural, spiritual, ideal and celestial. With this power he is enabled to overcome his lower, physical nature.

order.why: Read consciousness in relation to natural conditions.
Consider the distinction between sensation and the discovery of meanings.
Join development of the body with the cultivation of spiritual gifts.
shortened: Man thinks too much of perfecting the body, but of what use is it to him without the perfecting of the spirit?
But man is distinguished from the beast by his spiritual gifts and these he should develop with the other, both together.

order.why: Read the contrast of courage and fear in the public address.
Keep the reported comparison among mineral, vegetable, animal, and human realities.
Read the analogy of a complete body within its metaphysical argument.
Distinguish bodily life from the spiritual life described here.
shortened: Now, life is of two kinds: that of the body and that of the spirit. The life of the body consists in material life, but the life of the spirit is a heavenly existence which consists in receiving the grace of the Divine Spirit and being quickened through the breath of the Holy Spirit.

order.why: Consider the life-giving work attributed to the divine Spirit.
shortened: O maid-servant of God! The human spirit hath an impression and effect in the world, but the divine Spirit giveth life to the souls and confereth eternal life upon those who are attracted to the fragrances of God. This is the Great Cause from the Kingdom of thy Lord. Be attached to this New Spirit which hath effective power in the realities of things and creates new creatures.

order.why: Read Adam and Christ in the account of material and spiritual natures.
shortened: Answer:  Know that there are two natures in man:  the material and the spiritual.  The material nature is inherited from Adam, while the spiritual nature is inherited from the reality of the Word of God, which is the spirituality of Christ.  The material nature is born of Adam, but the spiritual nature is born of the grace of the Holy Spirit.  The material nature is the source of every imperfection and the spiritual nature is the source of all perfection.

order.why: Retain the related reported interpretation of Paul.
shortened: His Holiness St. Paul says, "You have died in Adam, you have become alive in the Christ. This statement is most significant. The purpose is this that in man there are two natures. One is material or physical. That is the heritage of Adam to man, for it is elemental; it is material; it belongs to earth. He is possessed of another nature, which is spiritual. That is Christ-like. That is born of the Word of God. That is from the Breaths of the Holy Spirit. That nature is radiant. That nature is heavenly, and that nature is divine.

order.why: Distinguish ordinary human planes from the three stations attributed to Manifestations.
shortened: Man has two planes: the physical and the intellectual. The divine revelators have three: their physical condition, which is shared by all mankind - they eat, they sleep, they are sometimes ill, they become well again, they become fatigued, they undergo all that man can undergo; their intellectual degree and their holy reality which surrounds all beings and comprehends secrets. Their horizons enfold the universe, for they are the suns of real truth illuminating all the regions of thought, dispersing the darkness, uplifting the world of mankind and making the material world heavenly.

order.why: Keep the Bab’s address concerning two stations within its own theological context.
Read the Bab’s statement concerning His verses and their proof in its original setting.
Consider the public address’s two pathways.
Read the separately reported contrast between reliance on guidance and materialism.
shortened: There are two pathways which have been pointed out by the Heavenly Educators. The first is Divine Guidance and reliance upon the Manifestations of God. The other is the road of Materialism and reliance upon the senses. These roads lead in opposite directions. The first leads to the world of the Kingdom; the other ends in the world of human vices, and is contrary to the cause of Divine Guidance.

order.why: Keep the reported pairing of peace and war in its original rhetoric.
Consider differing orientations toward the material and heavenly worlds.
Read the soul’s orientation through the imagery of return.
shortened: O soul that yearneth for the Beloved! The worldly soul is closely bound to the world of dust and is far removed from the beauty of the celestial world. The divine soul is an intimate of the self-subsistent Lord and is privy to the world of mystery. The earthly soul returneth to the earth, whilst the divine soul returneth unto the Lord of lords.

order.why: Retain the reported account of light, knowledge, and spiritual advancement.
shortened: Everything save man has one condition, but man has two. The animal has one condition or nature, but man has the animal nature (human) and the Divine nature (spiritual). If the Divine nature predominates he will be good, but if the human nature predominates he will be evil.

Man has the power of knowledge which will exalt him to Heaven, and the power of ignorance which will debase him to the lowest condition. The more the person advances in Divine things, the more will he receive the Attributes of Light; and the more he retrogrades, the more will he receive the attributes of darkness.

order.why: Read the separately reported struggle for direction of the soul.
Consider the reported distinction between kinds of love.
shortened: Material love is divided into two kinds - the animal and the human love. The animal loves its kind, the bird loves its mate and the gentle dove its offspring. Thus the human being has this quality and a greater power besides. Animal love has no permanent foundation and will soon pass away, but the human being sometimes loves for the sake of God and this another kind of love.

order.why: Read spiritual nourishment alongside the body’s food and drink.
shortened: Man has two aspects; a spiritual and an animal aspect. His animal side is sustained through food and drink like unto other beasts but his spiritual life is fed by the ideal perfections, faith, assurance, the Knowledge of God, and the Love of God.

order.why: Consider the paired images of sleep and waking, infancy and maturity.
shortened: Man is possessed of two stations: One is that of sleep and one of wakefulness. One is that of infancy, and one of maturity. One is that of utter helplessness and one is that of great assistance. One is that of utter poverty and one is absolute wealth. These are the two stations of man.

order.why: Close the linked readings with discernment among truth, love, education, and justice.
shortened: You know which path to follow: you cannot be mistaken, for there's a great distinction between God and evil, between Light and darkness, Truth and falsehood, Love and hatred, Generosity and meanness, Education and ignorance, Faith in God and superstition, good Laws and unjust laws.

order.why: Retain the supplied pilgrim note on the spirit’s two capacities.
Distinguish personal identity from ego in the supplied explanation.
End with the supplied Plotinian image of humanity poised between directions.

questions: Which qualities make the direction of a person’s inner life visible in ordinary conduct?
How do the images of two wings and competing tendencies illuminate different aspects of human development?
What helps intellect guide desire rather than become a clever instrument of it?
What similarities and differences emerge between Galatians 5:16–23 and the virtues named in this compilation?
How might education and repeated habits strengthen kindness, trustworthiness, and justice without encouraging contempt for oneself or others?
How do the connected subjects help distinguish spiritual growth, personal identity, bodily life, and responsibility for one’s choices?

references.label: 1 · Galatians 5:16–23 · Conflicting desires and spiritual fruit
references.note: The King James Version contrasts the works of the flesh with the fruit of the Spirit, including love, patience, gentleness, and self-restraint. Compare the moral direction expressed in these images with the guide’s accounts of higher and lower tendencies, while attending to each text’s own theological setting.

subjects.displayTitle: Evanescence and enduring life: what remains when self recedes?
subjects.introduction: Whoever becomes more evanescent becomes more lasting, Bahá’u’lláh writes, and whoever becomes poorer becomes richer. The mystics called the two sides of this paradox faná and baqá, passing away and abiding, and the Bahá’í writings take up their boldest images without flinching: the drop lost in the sea, the shadow that cannot survive the sun, the iron that takes on the fire’s heat, the dead body in the hands of the washer. Then they explain what the images mean, and the meaning is both humbler and more demanding than mystical union. No one’s will ever merges with God’s; the glory of existence is to let one’s own will fade into His, to have no desire but His desire, and to move by His command with joy. That dying, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá insists, shows itself in love and kindness, peace toward all humanity, and a servitude so complete that it asks no distinction. The Qur’án’s verse that all things perish save the face of God [1] sounds through this teaching as its ground and its promise. What remains when the self recedes is not emptiness but a larger life, and the path from here runs through the sacrifice of self, the question of existence and nonexistence, the hope of reunion with God, and the slow work of spiritual transformation.
subjects.arc: Begin with the paradox of becoming lasting through selflessness, clarify surrender and transcendence, then explore mystical images through service, humility, and transformed relationships.

order.why: Enter the Seven Valleys’ account of poverty and dying to self.
shortened: This station is that of dying to the self and living in God, of being poor in self and rich in the Desired One. Poverty, as here referred to, signifieth being poor in that which pertaineth to the world of creation and rich in what belongeth to the realms of God.

order.why: Open with the paradox of becoming more lasting and richer through evanescence and poverty.
shortened: Whosoever becometh more evanescent becometh more lasting, and whosoever becometh poorer becometh richer.

order.why: Read the explicit explanation in terms of forgetting selfish conditions.
shortened: 7. Evanescence and humility: That is to say man must become evanescent in God - must forget his own selfish conditions that he may thus arise to the station of sacrifice.

order.why: Clarify self-surrender through joyful action according to divine commands.
shortened: O Shaykh, O thou who hast surrendered thy will to God! By self-surrender and perpetual union with God is meant that men should merge their will wholly in the Will of God, and regard their desires as utter nothingness beside His Purpose. Whatsoever the Creator commandeth His creatures to observe, the same must they diligently, and with the utmost joy and eagerness, arise and fulfill.
The station of absolute self-surrender transcendeth, and will ever remain exalted above, every other station.

order.why: Distinguish the fading of personal will from a claim of union with the divine Essence.
shortened: Furthermore, no one's will hath ever been or shall ever be united with God's will, for the will of all hath been and shall ever be as nothingness before His will. The glory of existence is for one to make his own will fade away in God's will - that is, to have no will, thought or imagination of his own, but to move by God's will and act accordingly.

order.why: Read the limited purpose of the self beside the ocean of divine purpose.
Connect the station with love, kindness, peace, and harmony toward humanity.
shortened: This station is achieved through detachment and attraction, through effacement and evanescence, through love and kindness, and through peace and harmony towards all humanity.

order.why: Hear the prayer for selflessness in service to the loved ones.
shortened: Help me to be selfless at the heavenly entrance of Thy gate, and aid me to be detached from all things within Thy holy precincts. Lord! Give me to drink from the chalice of selflessness; with its robe clothe me, and in its ocean immerse me. Make me as dust in the pathway of Thy loved ones, and grant that I may offer up my soul for the earth ennobled by the footsteps of Thy chosen ones in Thy path, O Lord of Glory in the Highest.

order.why: Read the City of Absolute Nothingness with its shadow-and-sun image.
shortened: In this station, this most exalted habitation, this journey of utter self-effacement, the wayfarer forgetteth his soul, spirit, body, and very being, immerseth himself in the sea of nothingness, and liveth on earth as one unworthy of mention. Nor will one find any sign of his existence, for he hath vanished from the realm of the visible and attained unto the heights of self-abnegation.
How can a true lover continue to exist when once the effulgent glories of the Beloved are revealed? How can the shadow endure when once the sun hath shone forth?

order.why: Attend to the passage’s own explanation of its demanding image through qualities and action.
Read abiding in God through the stated meaning of seeking His will.
shortened: We have heard thy call and have remembered thee with these sublime words: In this Day, they who attribute themselves to God must be seen as evanescent in themselves and abiding in God - that is, they must seek no desire save His desire and move according to His Will and Purpose.

order.why: Retain the concise explanation connecting desire with divine purpose.
shortened: O My Name! Thy will must be connected to what God willeth, and thy desire must be annihilated in His desire - that is, thou must regard God's will as thy desire and His wish as thy purpose.

order.why: Consider receiving a binding divine command as beloved.
Read affirmation of what has descended from the divine will.
shortened: Blessed is he who hath caused his will to be annihilated in My will and hath attained to the affirmation of that which hath descended from the heaven of My will and flowed from My Pen.

order.why: Hear the counsel to set aside personal desire for what God desires.
shortened: O Abu-Talib! Fix thy gaze upon this blessed word which is as a crown for the head of mystical understanding: "Set aside what thou desirest and take what thy Lord desireth."

order.why: Read the meaning of Rida through good pleasure and purpose.
Consider the lover’s good pleasure within the language of surrendered desire.
shortened: For after the servant is effaced in the good-pleasure of the Worshipped One and the good-pleasure and desire of the lover is erased in the decree of the Beloved, the servant's good-pleasure becomes identical to the good-pleasure of the Worshipped One, and the Beloved's good-pleasure becomes the very reality of the lover's good-pleasure.

order.why: Hear prayer for action and speech aligned with divine purpose.
Read hope, deed, purpose, and remembrance joined in one prayer.
shortened: O Lord! Make my hope Thy remembrance, my deed Thy praise, my purpose Thy purpose, and my good-pleasure Thy good-pleasure, that I may be effaced from myself and endure through Thy Name, the Ever-Abiding, the Everlasting, the Mighty, the All-Wise.

order.why: Consider the prayer for attraction and hope in what is ordained.
shortened: Then attract him through the melodies of the Source of Thy Revelation to such a station wherein he may become wholly annihilated in Thy good-pleasure and hopeful of what Thou hast ordained in Thy tablets.

order.why: Read the interpretation of mystical words through servitude.
shortened: This servant says that the true meaning and the reality of meanings and the innermost secret of these verses, words and poetry is servitude at the Holy Threshold of the Most Glorious Beauty and utter effacement, evanescence and extinction at the Sacred Court.

order.why: Retain the concise linking of mystery, service, and self-effacement.
shortened: The secret of divine mysteries and the divine secret is servitude at the threshold and self-effacement and evanescence.

order.why: Consider purity of intention among the requirements of servitude.
shortened: O thou who standest in the stations of servitude! The requirements of servitude are purity of intention and complete effacement and self-abnegation. That is, in all conditions one must manifest absolute effacement, utter poverty and complete sacrifice, such that no trace or vestige of one's existence and being remaineth.

order.why: Read humility as healing from the maladies of self.
shortened: One should be the quintessence of humility, the very essence of meekness and be evanescence itself, healed of the maladies of the self.

order.why: Keep the stringent warning about distinction and uniqueness in its own admonitory voice.
shortened: When any soul perceiveth an existence for himself and imagineth a distinction and uniqueness, this is from the effects of croaking and a sign of hypocrisy. One must forget one's own conditions and attain to the station of utter evanescence, otherwise the observation of existence will ultimately lead to misbelief and manifest infidelity.

order.why: Consider the reported indifference to fame or obscurity.
shortened: Thus fame or oblivion, honor or degradation are one and the same to those Gems of existence. Indeed, their ultimate desire is selfless devotion to the one true God and absolute nothingness in His court.

order.why: Hear the prayer to retain only the designation of service.
shortened: O Lord! Preserve me from every title, attribute and name that may be uttered by the tongue of Thy loved ones, save the word that signifies servitude to Thy Baha and the sign that indicates evanescence and extinction before the manifestation of any of Thy signs.

order.why: Read the writer’s task through service and the quoted image of immortality.
shortened: Your pen must be the interpreter of this servant's pen, and whatever flows from this pen must stream from that pen - that is, in mentioning this servant's servitude, your pen will, God willing, become a mighty sign. This is what He says: "Until you are annihilated from the description of existence, O wayfarer, how can you taste the wine of immortality from the sweet ruby lips of the Beloved?"

order.why: Consider the poetic invitation to compose expressions of servitude.
Read effective teaching through enkindlement and humility.
shortened: The teacher, when teaching, must be himself fully enkindled, so that his utterance, like unto a flame of fire, may exert influence and consume the veil of self and passion. He must also be utterly humble and lowly so that others may be edified, and be totally self-effaced and evanescent so that he may teach with the melody of the Concourse on highâ€"otherwise his teaching will have no effect.

order.why: Consider selflessness in relation to the education of others.
Read character education as a setting for relinquishing self-centered desire.
shortened: Now character education must also be done in America so that souls may appear who are truly worthy and deserving of the Blessed Cause - who are completely effaced and evanescent, who are detached from self and passion and have withdrawn from their own desires, who have abandoned their own will and acquiesced to the Will of God, who, like the holy souls of Iran, shine forth from the horizon of the love of God and hasten to the field of sacrifice with utmost joy and delight.

order.why: Hear joy in friends whose service is self-effacing.
Read shared service through the image of one voice and melody.
Consider a personal prayer for devoted service.
Read enduring life through continuing to call others toward the All-Merciful.
Hear the request to praise while becoming forgetful of self.
Consider prostration as an expression of humility.
shortened: O thou who prostrateth thyself at the threshold of the Ancient Beauty!
Prostration is evidence of the absence of being--that is, of utter humility, evanescence and nothingness.

order.why: Read the station described as complete self-surrender.
Join assurance of heart with remembrance and poverty.
Consider the dervish’s poverty through the radiance of spiritual wealth.
Read the vanishing shadow as a sign of the sun’s appearance.
Consider the heated iron as an image of acquired attributes.
Read the enkindled candle’s consuming as a devotional image of enduring life.
Follow the image of a drop lost in the ocean of love.
Read ray, drop, and lover as related images of return.
shortened: Release yourselves from this world's life, and at every stage long ye for non-existence; for when the ray returneth to the sun, it is wiped out, and when the drop cometh to the sea, it vanisheth, and when the true lover findeth his Beloved, he yieldeth up his soul.

order.why: Contrasts ephemeral being with eternity and warns against imagined spiritual attainment.
Consider nothingness inscribed upon the heart as an opening to existence.
Read the reciprocal gates of extinction and immortality with the Quranic allusion.
shortened: Extinction is the gate to immortality, and immortality the gate to extinction. Non-existence is the door to existence, and existence the door to non-existence. The blessed word "All things shall perish save His Face" is a source of patience and solace for the peoples of the world.

order.why: Hear the brief affirmation of the One who abides.
shortened: Do not spur on your charger in pursuit of a shadow, for all shades and shadows are non existent. The only abiding one is He whose shade overshadoweth the world of eternity.

order.why: Distinguish what passes away from what abides with God.
shortened: Drink from the wine of love and close thine eyes to the world, for whatever thou seest will perish and pass away in an instant, while that which is with God remaineth and perisheth not, and endureth and fadeth not away.

order.why: Explore the passage’s stations and mystical claims in their own theological setting.
shortened: Therefore one must lift one's foot from the realm of nothingness and step into the realm of eternity, so that we may raise the banner of being in the heaven of non-being and comprehend the meaning of "All things perish save His face," and pass beyond the earthly homeland to return to the original divine homeland, of which "Verily we are God's and to Him we return" is indicative.

In this station and rank, existence is effaced from self and subsists through the Truth. All are from God and unto God shall they return, and "Say: All things are from God" is sufficient witness and adequate proof of this point, as the mystic of Rum has said:

His attributes are annihilated in the attributes of Him
While His essence remains through the survival of His essence

order.why: Read the poem’s movement beyond separation and union.
Follow the sequence from wonderment and submission to eternal life.
Consider the cupbearer after the stations of annihilation.
Read the poem of spiritual return and eternity.
shortened: One must set one's heart upon the eternal kingdom and pass beyond the mortal dust, that perchance on spiritual wings one may fly to the divine holy nest, there to sing with wondrous Iraqi melody this song of spiritual glory: We are all drunk with annihilation, We are all the light of glory, We are all the spirit of eternity.

order.why: Hear the overflowing sea and unrestrained pen as images of love.
Consider the phoenix’s flight beyond limiting conditions.
Read outward form and inward meaning within its account of beginning and end.
Consider the relation between immortal perception and immortal beauty.
shortened: Yea, an immortal ear is needed to hear the immortal Word, and an immortal eye is needed to behold the immortal Beauty, for that which is evanescent hath no path into the arena of eternity that it may comprehend the degrees of everlasting glory, and the abject one hath no portion of the cup of glory that he may step into His holy court.

order.why: Hear the confession of finite inability to praise the Eternal adequately.
Read evanescence and powerlessness beside permanence and might.
Keep the Bab’s prayer concerning remembrance and self-mention in its own voice.
shortened: How can I mention any but Thee, O my Beloved, after Thou hast given me to drink of the water of life in Thy knowledge? And how can I mention myself and its conditions after my awareness of Thy Being and Thy manifestations? By Thy might! It beseemeth not the non-existent to mention non-existence before Thy Ancient Self, O Everlasting One!

order.why: Consider prayer that exceeds syllables and sound.
shortened: Reveal then Thyself, O Lord! by Thy merciful Utterance and the mystery of Thy Divine Being, that the holy ecstasy of prayer may fill our souls -- a prayer that shall rise above words and letters and transcend the murmur of syllables and sounds -- that all things may be merged into nothingness before the revelation of Thy Splendour.

order.why: Read the prayer’s sea, pearls, and fruit as images of enduring bounty.
Hear absorption in the Beloved through the language of mercy.
Retain the brief account of intensified love.
Consider the striking claim about anger and forgiveness at the wayfarer’s station.
shortened: When the wayfarer reaches this most exalted and supreme station, firstly no anger arises in him that he should need to suppress it, and no self remains that should need to forgive.

order.why: Read the prayer against losing light after spiritual ascent.
shortened: In God alone do we seek refuge from a falling off after this bright ascent, from ashy sleep after enkindlement, from a darkness after having seen the light and from a veiling once again after the blessed sight of God's own mysteries.

order.why: Consider confidence in divine permanence amid vicissitudes.
shortened: If the pure handmaidens and assured believers were certain of the existence and permanence of God, they would not fear their own non-existence and evanescence, nor would they be saddened by any vicissitudes.

order.why: Hear the challenge to seek what gives lasting fruit.
shortened: Whatever you do and show forth and strive and boil and cry out, you will become like those who came before - meaning no trace or fruit will remain enduring and established - unless you become bewildered by that Beauty and yearning for that brilliant Moon.

order.why: Read longing to move from multiplicity toward a life-giving expanse.
shortened: The reality of existence hopes for the stations of witnessing, and the essence and being of existence longs for nonexistence and annihilation, that perchance through the grace and bounty of the Peerless Lord it may be freed from this world of multiplicity and find its way into the life-giving expanse of the Lord and be guided to the Kingdom of sanctification.

order.why: Consider yearning for reunion in the language of ascent.
Keep the intense devotional longing for return in its particular prayer.
Read the imagery of melting in love as part of this mystical vocabulary.
shortened: This is the arena of self-annihilation, of a hundred thousand acts of self -immolation, of being melted in pure love.

order.why: Consider the paradoxical pairing of annihilation and immortality in its devotional setting.
Read the sacrifice imagery through the passage’s own explanation of poverty and evanescence.
Retain the aspiration to follow the righteous exemplar.
shortened: I hope that we may attain to this station, become utterly effaced and non-existent, completely annihilated and obliterated, so that we may follow the example of that leader of the righteous ones and emerge from the realm of immortality, the supreme horizon, and the Most Glorious Kingdom.

order.why: Consider learning the way through hidden pearls and gems.
shortened: We should enlighten our eyes by observing the gleaming of its hidden pearls and treasured gems, and learn the way of non-existence and evanescence and effacement and obliteration.

order.why: Read servitude and return together at the described station.
shortened: For in that station the wayfarer, through the obliteration of multiplicity and the power of extinction, becomes free from all qualities of the Incomparable Lord and utters the words "We are God's and unto Him do we return." His existence is witness to Him, his servitude is his praiseworthy station, and complete annihilation is his ultimate goal.

order.why: Retain the appreciation of self-effacement conveyed in a letter.
Hear the call to joy in the covenant’s bounty.
Read the movement through heights and depths of self-effacement.
shortened: Sometimes you will hasten to the heights of evanescence, sometimes you will race into the depths of effacement and nothingness.

order.why: Consider intoxication as the image of service and selflessness.
shortened: But now thou art intoxicated with this cup and art a wine-worshipper in the tavern of servitude and self-effacement.

order.why: Hear the promised cup offered by the cupbearer of eternity.
shortened: Ere long shall ye drink the cup of evanescence from the hand of the cupbearer of eternity, and quaff the chalices of love from the hand of the celestial maiden.

order.why: Read the affirmation of an enduring existence.
Consider the addressee’s love, supplication, and turning toward God.
shortened: O distinguished and outspoken one! I have intoned the verses of your love which speak of your turning to God, your supplication to the Kingdom of God, your clinging to the hem of the robe of grandeur, your partaking of the choice wine of guidance, and your submergence in the sea of evanescence in God.

order.why: Hear the repeated appeal as an expression of devotional intensity.
shortened: Evanescence, evanescence, evanescence! Annihilation, annihilation, annihilation! This is the magnet that attracts divine confirmations.

order.why: Keep the reported comparison of preoccupations in its original voice.
Retain the reported concise paradox of evanescence and eternity.
shortened: When evanescent, you will become eternal. When evanescent, you will become everlasting.

order.why: Read the reported account of spiritual and worldly well-being in its religious setting.
shortened: For all people, from kings to subjects, eternal illumination, everlasting spirituality and perpetual existence lie in accepting the divine Cause, and likewise their worldly glory, comfort and freedom depend upon entering the divine Cause.

order.why: Keep the reported playful enumeration of things relinquished distinctly attributed.
shortened: One is to forfeit possessions, to forfeit estates. One is to forego name, honor, fame. One is to forsake relatives, station, Et Cetera, et cetera, (ended Abdul-Baha, laughing).

order.why: Close the linked readings with the imagery of the Bird and the seas of the Eternal.
shortened: The essential realities of the loved ones have perished from a single cry of the Bird of Divine Jealousy, and the radiant beings of the companions have ascended to the realm of evanescence from half a surge of the seas of the Presence of the Eternal.

order.why: Read the supplied al-Ghazali account of extinction from awareness of extinction.
End with the supplied poetic prayer of the drop seeking immortal life.

questions: How might becoming less preoccupied with oneself enlarge the capacity to love and serve?
What distinctions do the readings make between aligning one’s will with God’s and claiming to comprehend or unite with the divine Essence?
How do the drop, sea, candle, shadow, and heated iron illuminate different aspects of transformation?
What does Qur’an 28:88 add to the relationship between impermanence, divine command, and return?
How can mystical language of self-effacement be understood through concrete qualities such as humility, kindness, and peace?
What might remain of personal responsibility, individuality, and creative action when the demand for distinction recedes?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 28:88 · The passing of things and the enduring countenance
references.note: Read Pickthall’s translation and the parallel renderings of the verse, which joins the passing of all things with the divine countenance, command, and return to God. Compare its use within this compilation with the explanations of self-surrender and the distinction between divine permanence and contingent existence.

subjects.displayTitle: The visible world as a reflection of spiritual reality
subjects.introduction: Look at the world, Bahá’u’lláh says, and it will unfold the book of its own self before your eyes. The heavens tell of sovereign power, the sea of wealth, the wind of nearness; the leaves of a tree are pages, and a calligrapher is told that deeds and conduct are the lines on an unfurled scroll. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá adds a necessary caution. To call the visible world a reflection, a mirage beside the reality of God, is not to call it nothing; in its own degree it exists, as an image in a mirror has a real person standing behind it. A reflection points beyond itself, and every likeness has its limits. The practical question is what such perception does to a life: whether a heart that reads signs in rain and growth learns gratitude, whether a community can become a mirror of the realm above, whether the earth, a workshop rather than a gallery, can refine character. The Qur’an, turning rain into drink, pasture and crops, calls that provision a sign for people who reflect [1]. From here the road runs toward the two books of creation and revelation, the human reality fashioned in the image of God, and the spiritual springtime in which an outward season answers an inward one.
subjects.arc: Begin with the world as a readable book, distinguish relative reality from illusion, and move through natural images and spiritual correspondence toward worship, character, and shared action.

order.why: Explore the universe as a scroll of names and attributes.
shortened: Then wilt thou observe that the universe is a scroll that discloseth His hidden secrets, which are preserved in the well-guarded Tablet. And not an atom of all the atoms in existence, not a creature from amongst the creatures but speaketh His praise and telleth of His attributes and names, revealeth the glory of His might and guideth to His oneness and His mercy: and none will gainsay this who hath ears to hear, eyes to see, and a mind that is sound.

order.why: Enter the prayer through its heavens, seas, winds, and tree.
shortened: Whensoever I raise mine eyes to the heavens and witness their loftiness, I recognize naught therein but the wondrous heights of Thy supreme power and sovereign authority.

And whensoever, O my God, I behold the sea and its waves, methinks I hear the billowing ocean of Thy wealth and power. In the sun I discern naught but the marvellous splendour of the light of Thy hallowed countenance and presence, and in the wind I sense naught save the stirring breezes of Thy nearness and reunion. In the trees I behold only the revelation of the fruits of Thy wisdom and knowledge, and in their leaves I read but the pages of the books enshrining the mysteries of all that hath been through Thy command or will be through Thy power.

order.why: Open with the invitation to ponder the world as a book.
Establish that relative existence need not mean sheer illusion.
shortened: This notion is false, for although the existence of things is an illusion compared to the existence of God, yet in the contingent world it is established, proven, and undeniable.
It is therefore evident that although created things have no existence compared to that of God, being instead like a mirage or an image reflected in a mirror, yet in their own degree they exist.

order.why: Consider a reported everyday example of speech producing inner effects.
Read the two books of creation and revelation together.
shortened: The verse concerns this: there are two unfurled books - one the Book of Creation and the other the Book of Revelation. The Book of Revelation comprises the heavenly scriptures revealed unto the divine Prophets and issued from the pure mouth of Truth. The Book of Creation is this preserved tablet of contingent being and the unfurled scroll of existence, and Creation follows Revelation.

When thou readest Revelation, thou becomest aware of divine mysteries, and when thou gazest upon the Book of Creation, thou beholdest the signs, symbols, realities, conditions and manifestations of the hidden mystery and the outpourings of the Incomparable Lord.

order.why: Retain the related contrast between scripture and the horizons.
shortened: The former were inscribed in books, psalms, scrolls and tablets, while the latter appeared in the Preserved Tablet and the outstretched parchment of the horizons.

order.why: Turn toward careful observation of creation.
shortened: O namesake of the Most Desired One! Open the eye of outward vision in the arena of existence, that thou mayest behold the verses of the Supreme Concourse inscribed, recorded and confirmed in clear script upon the scroll of the horizons. And observe with care the pure and delicate pages of creation, that thou mayest perceive the images of the most glorious Kingdom.

order.why: Connect the image of writing with the lines formed by deeds.
shortened: O Calligrapher! This world of being is an inscribed book and an unfurled scroll.
These lines are deeds and actions, ways and words and conduct.

order.why: Join the inward temple of the heart with outward worship and action.
shortened: I ask God to make the heart of every one of you a temple of the Divine Temples and to let the lamp of the great guidance be lighted therein; and when the hearts find such an attainment, they will certainly exert the utmost endeavor and energy in the building of the Mashrak-el-Azcar; thus may the outward express the inward, and the form (or letter) indicate the meaning (or reality).

order.why: Read the assembly’s unity through the removal of prejudice.
shortened: As for the Spiritual Assembly, I pray that God may assist them in all affairs and enable them to exalt the Word of God and promote the divine teachings, so that they may become the cause of human unity and the spread of the divine breaths, until no prejudice remains between religions, denominations and races, and all may hold fast together to the cord of God, and misunderstandings between all parties may vanish, and the human world may become a mirror of the Kingdom of God upon which spiritual lights shine.

order.why: Consider conduct as the reflection of teachings.
shortened: I hope that this may be so, meaning that the loved ones of God may conduct themselves according to the teachings, counsels and exhortations of Baha'u'llah, so that the lights of the Kingdom may be reflected in the mirror of the human world.

order.why: Read the garden’s visible flowers through the image of mystical learning.
shortened: Then came forth flowers of mystic learning, and, bespeaking the knowledge of God, fresh greenery from the ground. The contingent world displayed God's bounteous gifts, the visible world reflecting the glories of realms that were hidden from sight.

subjects.displayTitle: Literal and symbolic readings of scripture
subjects.introduction: Zion dances, the trees clap their hands, a dove descends, the sun goes dark. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá observes that every discipline has its own terminology and that scripture speaks a language of its own, which, read as plain report, becomes a wall between the reader and the One it promises. Bahá’u’lláh traces the pattern through history: people who waited for a Messiah from an unknown place, or for stars to fall from heaven, held so fast to the letter that they failed to recognise the fulfilment standing before them. Yet the same Writings insist that a clear and decisive text cannot be bent by conjecture, and expose the reader who interprets only to license what he already wants. The task is to read attentively enough to tell an image from an instruction, and a text’s purpose from inherited expectation. The temple saying in John’s Gospel, which the narrative itself unfolds as the body of Jesus, shows how a text can carry its own key [1]. From here the path leads into symbolism and the many layers of meaning in scripture, the limits of language itself, and the inner struggle that recognition demands.
